title: Matplotlib Exercises
description: Practise the ideas from this Matplotlib course. Each answer has an explanation to help you learn.

exercises.question: What is fig?
exercises.explanation: A figure is the whole chart image. An Axes object is an area inside it where data is drawn. The line passes through the three given points. fig refers to the image; ax refers to its plotting area.

exercises.question: Where should units be explained?
exercises.explanation: Axis labels explain what values mean and which units they use. A title tells the reader the chart's topic. The chart now explains both axes. A reader does not need to guess whether 4 means books, minutes or people.

exercises.question: Which activity has the most votes?
exercises.explanation: A bar chart compares categories. Bars usually start from zero so their lengths fairly represent the values. Music has the tallest bar because it has 5 votes.

exercises.question: What does each point represent?
exercises.explanation: A scatter plot shows paired measurements as separate points. It helps reveal a relationship without connecting every point. The three points show three paired observations. A pattern alone would not prove one value causes the other.

exercises.question: What does a bin group?
exercises.explanation: A histogram groups numbers into bins and counts how many fall in each bin. A bin is an interval, not a category label. The three bins have heights 2, 1 and 3. The explicit edges make the grouping clear.

exercises.question: What does a legend explain?
exercises.explanation: A legend matches a line or marker to its label. It is useful when one chart has more than one series. The legend tells which line belongs to each team.

exercises.question: What do y limits choose?
exercises.explanation: Axis limits choose the part of the number range shown. Use them deliberately and tell readers when a narrow range matters. The y-axis displays zero through 12, keeping the small differences in context.

exercises.question: How many plotting areas are created?
exercises.explanation: subplots can create several plotting areas. Give each area clear labels so readers can compare them correctly. The figure has one row and two plotting areas. The first is a bar chart; the second is a line chart.

exercises.question: Why use a light grid?
exercises.explanation: A light grid can help readers estimate values. It should support the data rather than overpower it. The grid is partly transparent, so the plotted line remains easy to see.

exercises.question: What does savefig produce?
exercises.explanation: savefig writes the figure to a file. Choose a format and size appropriate for how it will be used. A PNG image is saved in the current working directory. Closing the figure releases its resources.

exercises.question: Does a missing value mean zero?
exercises.explanation: Missing data should not be silently shown as a real zero. A gap can honestly show that no observation was recorded. The missing middle value breaks the line. It is not plotted as zero.

exercises.question: How many more books are shown on Tuesday?
exercises.explanation: A chart should answer a clear question without exaggerating. Check title, units, scale and the underlying values before sharing. The title states the data is fictional. The zero-based scale shows a difference of one book.
